title: Personal Agent Pattern: Agent Privilege path
lede: One person, one agent. The Ping Agentic Control Plane decides at three points: who the user is (Agent IAM Core), which tools the agent may use (Agent Privilege, which is also the MCP front door) and what the business rules allow (Agent Authorize).

steps.title: asks
steps.what: The user asks their personal agent for something. The agent is theirs; it acts for one person.

steps.title: prompt
steps.what: The agent uses a language model to decide which tool to call. The model never holds a credential.

steps.title: User authenticates
steps.what: The user signs in through Agent IAM Core. The agent receives a token whose audience is the MCP gateway and whose subject is the user.

steps.title: MCP / OIDC, tool check
steps.what: The agent calls Agent Privilege over MCP with that token. Agent Privilege applies tool-level (coarse to medium grained) authorization: may this user, through this agent, call this tool at all?

steps.title: OBO (coming soon)
steps.what: Not available yet. When it is, Agent Privilege will swap the token for an on-behalf-of token for the MCP server (same subject), and it depends on MCP support. Until then the next call uses the credential the MCP server accepts.

steps.title: MCP
steps.what: Agent Privilege uses the credential that server needs: OIDC, a static token or an API key.

steps.title: API call
steps.what: The MCP server calls the backend through the API gateway.

steps.title: Fine grained
steps.what: Agent Authorize applies finer-grained, business-level rules to this request and data.

steps.title: allowed call
steps.what: Only a request that passed both layers reaches the resource.
